question: A shop sells 40% of its stock in a sale, then 40% of what is left the next week. What share is gone?
answer: The second 40% is of the remaining 60%, so it clears 24%. Forty plus twenty-four is sixty-four per cent gone, and thirty-six left. Percentages of percentages never add.
move: Two forty-per-cent cuts leave more than a fifth standing.
trap: Adding two percentages that are taken of different things.
